layer_production_hostinger.load_attribution: Whole shared node across tenant accounts, not this account. This account ran 6 lsphp processes, each at 0.0 %CPU at capture time.

deploy_discipline.verdict: keep-only-previous-version discipline holds; no deploy hoarding

mail_jobs.interpretation: Deliberate incident holds from the 2026-10-22 event, preserved by NotificationHold. Not a new accumulation and not a dead-letter pile.

action_scheduler.verdict: No overdue work, no stuck claims, no pending mail attempts. Production queue is healthy.

layer_production_engine_vps.verdict: Exactly one process per service, no accumulation, load near idle on a single core.

layer_local_snapshots_and_backups.large_site_copies_note: Each dates from a specific finished task; none carries a current owner or deadline. Recorded as over-limit, not deleted, because this session is evidence-only.

mechanism_ledger.status: INEFFECTIVE - FIX NOT PRESENT IN MAIN

before.source: PR #1063 description, measured on the review instance 2026-11-10

actual_main_state.commit_shape: 521843db8 'fix(mail): terminate exhausted and orphaned mail jobs' (+22/-0 across 14 files) followed by 985bf4c0d 'fix(tests): align InternalSmtpTest expectations' which removes 459 lines, reverting the fix and keeping only test deletions

reproduction_today.offset_note: The absolute next_slot is the stable figure (oldest of the 64 retained entries + 24 h). The hour offset shrinks as wall-clock time advances; recomputing later yields a smaller offset against the same next_slot.
reproduction_today.method: Read linker_c222.wp_options.linker_commerce_mail_transport_sends, applied the live Throttle::slot() formula from main (PER_DAY 80 - PHP_RESERVE 16 = 64)

production_state.budget_entries: not saturated at capture; mail_attempt pending 0, failed 0
production_state.why: Production inquiry volume is low and the 38 held jobs never re-enter the throttle
production_state.risk: The same saturation is reachable in production under any burst that reaches 64 PHP sends in 24 h

mechanism_ledger.conclusion: The 'after' numbers in PR #1063 describe code that does not exist in main or production. They must not be counted as evidence of an effective mechanism. The defect is live and reproduced.

mechanism_ledger.claim: Orphaned planner worker processes bound to a dead instance are reconciled on stop/start (PR #1036, issue #1030)

before.observation: `just down` left an orphaned worker_host serve python child alive; pid file recorded only the uv parent. Orphan kept polling a stale execution identity and let an admitted weather run sit unclaimed through its 120s deadline.

after.observation: stop() also stops any live worker_host serve bound to the instance (TERM-first, shared stop grace); start() clears untrack state.

today_check.binding_check: Read LINKER_PLANNER_CONFIG from each worker's environment and matched it to an instance whose PHP, engine and genie ports are all still listening.

mechanism_ledger.conclusion: Three workers, three distinct live instances, zero orphans. This is a stronger check than counting processes: the binding that #1036 keyed on is intact for every worker.

mechanism_ledger.claim: Action Scheduler backlog and mail queue stay bounded in production

before.observation: no production resource emergency; node load is other tenants'

mechanism_ledger.conclusion: Queue bounded, nothing overdue, no stuck claims. Effective.

mechanism_ledger.claim: Only the previous code generation is retained on the host
mechanism_ledger.conclusion: Atomic-switch rollback point is a single generation. Effective.

mechanism_ledger.claim: Local dev instances stay within the local-storage.md boundary
mechanism_ledger.conclusion: Not a mechanism that has been proven; the boundary is exceeded — 58 resident copies for 3 running instances. Reclamation is a separate decision for the owner.
Rotation exists (.snapshot-retention.json) but the count exceeds the documented boundary. Evidence-only here.

mechanism_ledger.claim: CI dependency caches are bounded and retired with closed PRs
mechanism_ledger.conclusion: Bounded growth with an automatic retirement path. Effective.

mechanism_ledger.claim: Account-level CPU on the shared host stays low regardless of node-wide load
mechanism_ledger.conclusion: Consistent with the 2026-11-10 baseline; the node figure is other tenants' work and outside our control. No action threshold crossed.

honest_gaps: Only one production sample was taken today; the 'before' for M1 is the PR's own numbers, which describe removed code, so M1 has no valid before/after pair at all.

No production burst was induced to force budget saturation; the reproduction is on a local instance. Production saturation remains a hypothesis backed by an identical formula and an identical 64-entry ledger shape.
The 38 held jobs on production were not released or deleted; this session was read-only. Whether they should be released is an owner decision.
Local instance and snapshot over-limit findings were not remediated; reclamation is out of scope for an evidence-only baseline.

A first pass of this document claimed zero running local instances because the process filter misspelled the actual command line. The corrected figures come from reading LINKER_PLANNER_CONFIG per worker and matching listening ports to the registry; the wrong version never left this branch.
